summary: 2D screening label: not_2d_applicable. Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped). The gate blocked it because the custom_2d_steady experiment has no blocks and no power_w object (needs 1–128 blocks), so input validity failed. simulation_allowed is false, comparison_valid is false, and the scientific gate and independent verification both failed. The scenario is a custom 2D steady run with no transient trace. It is not a bundled EV6/GCC adapted demonstration. It is also not a pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace illustrative input, so there is no generated placement, no source commit, no input.flp and no one-row input.ptrace. The paper (W2910207760) describes leakage-aware dynamic thermal management of a 16-core chip with piecewise-linear model predictive control. It uses a 1 s control step, a 1 ms golden plant step, an 80 C target, a 40 C ambient and time-varying Wattch/SPEC power. Its reported observable is an average tracking difference of 0.78 degC (maximum 1.16 degC; traditional MPC 1.32 average and 5.97 maximum) for Nc=1, Np=2 and 5 expansion points. No Studio result exists, so no numerical comparison is made. The paper's tracking error measures closed-loop controller behavior around a target. A steady 2D temperature field would be a different quantity, and the paper does not state the averaging scope over cores and time. Any reading of this scenario is limited to qualitative sensitivity: leakage-temperature feedback, controller horizon and expansion-point choices affect tracking accuracy in the paper, which a static solver cannot reproduce. No exact replication is claimed and the final verdict follows the gate.
limitations: Studio did not run: the input is invalid (no floorplan blocks, no power_w) and the verdict is not_2d_applicable, so there is no Studio output to assess.
comparison_valid is false; the 0.78 degC average tracking difference and the 1.16 degC maximum cannot be compared numerically with any Studio quantity.
Mismatch in regime: the paper is a transient closed-loop DTM with a 1 s control step and a 1 ms plant step; the screened experiment is steady-state with no transient trace.
Mismatch in observable and aggregation: the paper reports a tracking error against an 80 C target with unspecified averaging over cores and time; a steady 2D solve gives a spatial temperature field.

Mismatch in physics: nonlinear exponential leakage feedback (TSMC 65 nm, PWL-approximated, iterated golden plant) and a closed-form regularized least-squares MPC have no counterpart in a fixed-power thermal solve.
Mismatch in boundary and package assumptions: the paper uses a reduced-order RC network with unspecified package, cooling and material properties and a 40 C ambient; Studio assumptions are empty.

Missing inputs: Fig. 3 per-core coordinates and sizes, per-core watts, Wattch/SPEC power time series and core assignment, RC matrices, leakage parameters, and the final placement were not provided or digitized.
No pinned assets, code, configs or repository URLs were found (artifact search: checked_no_links), so no source commit or placement assumption can be reported.

The original study is a transient closed-loop DTM problem with a 1 s control step and a 1 ms plant step, using time-varying SPEC/Wattch power. A steady-state 2D solve with a one-row power trace cannot represent the controller, the predictive horizon or the transient overshoot behavior.
The controller is the main contribution (PWL MPC with Nc/Np horizons, power recommendations, DVFS and task-load adjustment). A static thermal solver has no equivalent.

The leakage-temperature feedback is nonlinear: an exponential subthreshold model, TSMC 65 nm process, PWL-approximated, with an iterated golden plant. A fixed-power thermal solve omits this coupling unless leakage is modeled separately.
The optimizer is a closed-form regularized least-squares MPC. A generic placement or thermal optimizer is not equivalent.

The paper reports a reduced-order RC network with sensor-based per-core outputs, and its package, cooling and interposer details are unspecified. The paper's temperatures (80 C target, 40 C ambient) cannot be compared numerically with any 2D Studio result.
The paper contains no 3D stack, interposer or chiplet structure and no reliability analysis beyond the falling-case range (120 to 80 C), so there is no 3D or interposer mismatch to resolve.
